text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Communist Party chief Do Muoi has called for increased cooperation between Vietnamese scientists living at home and abroad.
-- Ho Chi Minh City expects to collect $200 million in taxes from foreign invested firms this year.
-- The State Bank of Vietnam will present draft banking laws on the rights and obligations of creditors and borrowers to the next National Assembly session.
-- The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is seeking to simplify visa requirements for overseas Vietnamese.
-- Vietnam will auction some $2.68 million worth of one-year treasury bills on Wednesday.
-- Argentina and Vietnam signed accords on agricultural and science cooperation on Monday.
-- More than 3,700 people joined the Communist Party in Hanoi in 1996.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Khanh has told the visiting French Environment Minister that Vietnam is seeking French help with environmental protection in the country's two biggest cities.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet plans an official visit to India in March.
-- Schools in Ho Chi Minh City launched an anti-drug campaign on Monday.
